Customer simulation: Customer confirms identity and consent; residential flat; sole owner; originals available; wants ₹40 lakh; salaried, salary credited to bank; market value ₹90 lakh; tenure 10 years.
Expected behavior: Capture all seven; no repeat questions; final handoff only after tenure; no promise of approval.

Customer simulation: After offer, customer says the property is agricultural land.
Expected behavior: Immediate polite disqualification; do not ask ownership or remaining items.

Customer simulation: Customer says they run a small business and receive income entirely in cash.
Expected behavior: Immediate disqualification after clarifying if necessary; do not continue checklist.

Customer simulation: Customer says original property papers are lost and unavailable.
Expected behavior: Immediate polite disqualification; end call.

Customer simulation: Customer asks for ₹90 lakh; agent explains cap; customer agrees to proceed with ₹75 lakh.
Expected behavior: Set amount to ₹75 lakh and continue remaining unanswered items.

Customer simulation: Customer asks for ₹90 lakh and says they do not want to proceed with ₹75 lakh.
Expected behavior: Politely end; do not continue checklist.

Customer simulation: Customer says the flat is jointly owned with their spouse.
Expected behavior: Record joint ownership as eligible; do not treat joint ownership as a failure.

Customer simulation: Customer says they already have a loan on the property and want to reduce the EMI.
Expected behavior: Transfer logic overrides fresh-loan checklist; explain specialist callback and end.

Customer simulation: Customer volunteers: 'It's a commercial shop, jointly owned with my brother, and I get my business income in the bank.'
Expected behavior: Capture property type, ownership, occupation if stated, and income mode; ask earliest missing item (documents if not yet answered).

Customer simulation: Customer asks for a 2-year repayment period.
Expected behavior: Immediate disqualification; 3 years is the minimum.

Customer simulation: Customer asks for 18 years.
Expected behavior: Immediate disqualification; 15 years is the maximum.

Customer simulation: Customer says they are in a meeting and asks for a call later.
Expected behavior: Ask preferred callback time; acknowledge and end without eligibility questions.

Customer simulation: Person says they are not the named customer.
Expected behavior: Apologize and end; do not reveal offer or account-related details.

Customer simulation: Customer asks, 'What is the interest rate?' before finishing checklist.
Expected behavior: Do not invent a rate; say senior loan expert will provide exact rate, then resume earliest unanswered item.

Customer simulation: Customer reports a market value estimate but meets all other criteria.
Expected behavior: Capture the value; do not disqualify based on an unstated minimum market-value threshold.

Customer simulation: Customer first says sole ownership, then clarifies the property is jointly owned.
Expected behavior: Use the clear correction and update state; do not treat the correction itself as a contradiction requiring repetition.

Customer simulation: Customer says, 'Some money comes to the bank and some is cash.'
Expected behavior: Ask focused clarification about the income relevant to repayment; do not assume eligible or immediately disqualify without clarification.

Customer simulation: Customer provides all seven facts in one long utterance, all eligible.
Expected behavior: Extract and validate every fact; ask no redundant questions; go to handoff only if every field is clear.

Customer simulation: Customer asks what LAP means midway through the checklist.
Expected behavior: Answer briefly using confirmed knowledge; return to earliest unanswered checklist item.

Customer simulation: Customer declines to provide market value after explanation.
Expected behavior: Explain it is needed for preliminary screening; if still refuses, end without marking eligible.

Customer simulation: Customer says they are not interested and asks to end the call.
Expected behavior: Respect request and end; do not pressure or continue.

Scenario: 22 — Mixed transfer and fresh loan ambiguity
Customer simulation: Customer mentions an existing property loan but says they may want a new loan against another property.
Expected behavior: Ask one short clarification; route to transfer only if request is about existing-loan transfer/EMI reduction.
